data.gender_notes: Khagendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words ‘Khaga’ meaning 'god' and ‘Indra’ meaning 'lord of riches'. This name is believed to bring wealth, prosperity, and abundance. The name Khagendra carries the meaning “God of riches and prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Khagendra usually hope their child will grow to embody god of riches and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing divine blessings and material wealth.
data.etymology: Khagendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of riches and prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khagendra total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Khagendra" is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, honoring the deity Indra, who is the lord of rain, rivers, and thunderstorms. He is also considered as the king of gods and is renowned for his power and wealth. The name Khagendra carries all these attributes, evoking a sense of grandeur, power, and prosperity.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond its cultural significance, the name "Khagendra" also holds spiritual importance. The name Kimbhu (a variation of Khagendra) is found in Hindu scriptures, referring to Lord Vishnu's manifestation, who grants all forms of material desires and protects his devotees. Therefore, the name "Khagendra" signifies divine protection, prosperity, and spiritual growth. Wearing the name suggests being blessed by the gods, and it is a symbol of being a revered, powerful, and wealthy individual.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Khagendra: God of Time and Destiny. Symbolizes the eternal cycle of life and the wisdom to navigate its uncertainties.

historical_references.reference: Khagendra Nath Tara, a renowned Bengali poet, was born in 1884 in a small village in what is now Bangladesh. He was a key figure in the Bengali literary renaissance of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and is considered one of the greatest poets of modern Bengali literature.

Khagendra Nath Datta, also known as Lalon Fakir, was a 19th-century Bengali folk poet and saint. He was born in 1774 in the village of Chottogram in present-day Bangladesh and is considered to be the patron saint of the Sufi tradition in Bengal. His songs, which are still widely sung, are deeply spiritual and draw upon both Hindu and Muslim influences.
